title: Conditional active-slice extension criterion for generalized operads
statement:
Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, inert edges and algebra categories defined in [lem-coef-inert-operad-color-reconstruction]. Let $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads with $\mathcal A_{[0]},\mathcal B_{[0]}$ Kan complexes and $u_{[0]}$ an equivalence. Let $\mathcal V$ be a monoidal infinity category; no cocompleteness or presentability is assumed. A base arrow is active if its opposite preserves the two endpoints. For $b\in\mathcal B_{[1]}$, let
$$K_b=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b},$$
where $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{act}}$ is the wide subcategory of arrows over active base arrows. For an $\mathcal A$-algebra $A$, let $D_{A,b}:K_b\to\mathcal V$ send $(a,u(a)\to b)$, with $a$ over $[n]$ and successive inert colors $a_i$, to $\bigotimes_{i=1}^n A(a_i)$, with value $\mathbf1$ for $n=0$; arrows use the active algebra operations. Assume, for every $A,b$, that $D_{A,b}$ has a colimit preserved by $x\mapsto L\otimes x\otimes R$ for every pair of fixed objects $L,R\in\mathcal V$, allowing the tensor unit. Then restriction $u^*$ has a coherent left adjoint $u_!$ with
$$(u_!A)(b)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{K_b}D_{A,b},\qquad \operatorname{Map}(u_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,u^*B),$$
naturally in $A$ and every $\mathcal B$-algebra $B$. Its unit is induced by the identity-operation cocones; its operations are induced by substitution of active operations, compatibly with all higher homotopies.

Read online at https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/gepner-haugseng2.pdf; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

external.place: Proposition A.2.10, Propositions A.4.3–A.4.4 and Corollary A.4.5, printed pp.703,705–706

proof.text: Fix an $\mathcal A$-algebra $A$ and $b\in\mathcal B_{[1]}$. Put $T_b:K_b\to\mathcal A_{\mathrm{act}}\xrightarrow{A}\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$. The pullback and slice are small. The active arrows $u(a)\to b$ give a coherent transformation of the base of $T_b$ to the constant object $[1]$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], transport in the functor category gives a coherent cocartesian transformation $\lambda_b:T_b\to Q_b$, where $Q_b:K_b\to\mathcal V$ lies over $[1]$. The Segal and tensor-transport clauses of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] identify $Q_b(a,\alpha)$ with $D_{A,b}(a,\alpha)=\bigotimes_iA(a_i)$, with $\mathbf1$ at arity zero, and identify every simplex of $Q_b$ with the corresponding active algebra-operation simplex. Thus this is a construction of the whole coherent diagram, not just its vertices.

Choose the assumed colimit cocone $c_b:D_{A,b}\to\Delta v_b$ and compose it with the transport $\lambda_b$ from Step 1 to get an active cocone $T_b\to v_b$. For fixed tuples $P,Q$ let $L=\bigotimes P$, $R=\bigotimes Q$, with the unit for the empty tuple. The contextual diagram has arrows $\operatorname{id}_L\otimes D_{A,b}(f)\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ and cocone maps $\operatorname{id}_L\otimes c_b\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$. By assumption it is a colimit with apex $L\otimes v_b\otimes R$. Here is why this gives the operadic cocone condition of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. Concatenate each component of $\lambda_b$ with the identity maps of $P,Q$, over the block contraction $[p+n+q]\to[p+1+q]$. Factor this map through a cocartesian lift of that contraction using the mapping-space fiber formula of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Each inert projection of the intervening vertical comparison is an equivalence: it compares two transports of the same fixed factor or the same active middle block. The Segal equivalence of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] makes that comparison an equivalence, so the concatenated map is cocartesian. Apply the functor-category version of that transport formula to all of $K_b$, and then compose with transport to $[1]$. It identifies the space of active contextual cocones with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_b,\mathcal V)}(L\otimes D_{A,b}\otimes R,\Delta w)$, and contextual active maps out of the apex with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(L\otimes v_b\otimes R,w)$. Restriction is an equivalence by the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Empty $P$ or $Q$ therefore gives both required one-sided tests. This uses only the specified preserved colimits, including initial colimits when $K_b$ is empty.

Apply [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison] to $u$ to form $\mathcal M_u$. It is small, has source $\mathcal A$ and target $\mathcal B$, and is constant over $[0]$ by the assumed equivalence $u_{[0]}$ on Kan zero-fibers. Its color slice $J_b$ is $K_b$, with the same source diagram and induced cocones. Check also the whole-family stationary inert-lift requirement of [lem-coef-operadic-correspondence-kan-filling]. At parameter $0$, an inert lift in $\mathcal A$ maps by $u$ to an inert lift in $\mathcal B$. Mapping into an object of parameter $0$ tests its cocartesian square in $\mathcal A$; mapping into an object of parameter $1$ tests that of its image under $u$ by the collage mixed-mapping formula. Both squares are homotopy pullbacks. At parameter $1$, the test is the square in $\mathcal B$; maps backwards to parameter $0$ and their base fibers are empty. Thus the stationary lifts are cocartesian for the whole family by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The relative incidence-limit condition also follows from the collage comparison; explicitly, for an apex $x$ and an incoming test object $z$, when both lie in the same endpoint fiber its fixed-base mapping-space limit is precisely the relative-limit axiom of [lem-coef-inert-operad-color-reconstruction]. When $z$ lies in the source and $x$ in the target, the collage formula identifies the apex and every incidence mapping space with the corresponding spaces from $u(z)$ in $\mathcal B$, naturally in the incidence diagram, so the same target-fiber axiom applies. When $z$ lies in the target and $x$ in the source, all incoming spaces and their interval-base spaces are empty. The incidence diagram is nonempty, including the singleton vertex diagram at arity zero, so its fixed-base limit is empty as well. These cases verify the family hypothesis without imposing a new condition on $u$.

source.place: GH A.3.1--A.3.4 and Remark A.4.2; collage family and stationary inert lifts

proof.text: The noncolor and multi-input comparison is the following. For $x\in\mathcal B_{[r]}$, clause (i) of [lem-coef-operadic-active-incidence-comparison] applied to $\mathcal M_u$ identifies $J_x$ with $\prod_{i=1}^rJ_{x_i}$, respecting source diagrams and inert projection cones. All its hypotheses were checked in Step 3. The color cocones in Step 2 are stable in every simultaneous left and right context, exactly the strengthened hypothesis of [lem-coef-operadic-concatenation-colimits]. Thus their product has a concatenation cocone stable in all contexts, and in particular operadically colimiting, with tuple apex $(v_{x_1},\ldots,v_{x_r})$. It includes empty factors and $r=0$, where the source is contractible and the apex is the empty tuple. For an active map $\beta:x\to y$ to a color, postcomposition defines $J_x\to J_y$, $(a,\alpha)\mapsto(a,\beta\alpha)$, on the whole slice, with its commuting triangles and higher simplices. Restrict the color cocone at $y$ along this functor and along $\prod_iJ_{x_i}\simeq J_x$. It is a cocone on the product source diagram. The product-cocone universal property gives the induced operation from the tuple apex to $v_y$; under active tensor transport it is the map $\bigotimes_i v_{x_i}\to v_y$. For multiple outputs use their inert projections. This establishes the local operation formula; the coherent extension in the next step supplies its simultaneous compatibility on all simplices.

source.place: GH A.2.3--A.2.4; product of slices and product-indexed concatenation cocones

proof.text: The existence clause of [lem-coef-operadic-correspondence-kan-filling] now applies to $A$ on $\mathcal M_u$: each required color active diagram has the operadically colimiting cocone from Step 2, and the constant Kan zero-fiber and stationary inert hypotheses were verified in Step 3. It constructs an actual coherent inert-preserving functor $H:\mathcal M_u\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ restricting to $A$, which is an operadic left Kan extension. By [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison], $H$ is the data of a $\mathcal B$-algebra $F_A$ and an algebra transformation $\eta_A:A\to u^*F_A$, on all simplices. No independent choices of operation maps are asserted to assemble. The empty-context colimit condition, identified using [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], says that $D_{A,b}\to F_A(b)$ is a colimit cocone. Its unique colimit comparison identifies $F_A(b)$ with $v_b$ and their entire cocones. The leg at $(a,\operatorname{id}_{u(a)})$ is exactly $\eta_A(a)$. The operations of $H$ induce the substitution maps in Step 4, since both maps restrict to the same cocone on the product source diagram. The natural mapping-space equivalence of that product cocone identifies them with all higher homotopies. Since its ordinary color cocone is equivalent to the selected cocone preserved by every two-sided tensoring functor, the same contextual transport argument of Step 2 shows that the resulting color cocones are stable in all contexts as well.

source.place: GH Theorem A.3.4(i), Remark A.4.2, Corollary A.4.5; coherent operadic extension

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E=\mathcal E_{\mathcal M_u}(\mathcal V)$. For any $G\in\mathcal E$ with source restriction $Y$, restriction gives $\rho:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(H,G)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal V)}(A,Y)$. It lifts every boundary $\partial\Delta^n\subseteq\Delta^n$, including $n=0$: in the right-pinched mapping model of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the specified boundary consists of proper faces of $\Delta^{n+1}$ containing its final vertex $G$. Add its initial face as the constant simplex at $H$; this is the entire $\partial\Delta^{n+1}$. The prescribed base simplex gives compatible data on $\mathcal A\times\Delta^{n+1}$. Thus the domain is exactly the one in the relative boundary-lifting assertion of [lem-coef-operadic-correspondence-kan-filling], with $m=n+1>0$ and initial vertex $H$. Its filler preserves every prescribed face and gives the desired pinched simplex. At $n=0$ it gives the edge between the two prescribed vertices. The boundary characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes $\rho$ a trivial Kan fibration, hence an equivalence. This is the coherent algebra-map assembly, including all its higher simplices.

source.place: GH Theorem A.3.4(ii) and Proposition A.4.3; right-pinched mapping boundaries

proof.text:
For a $\mathcal B$-algebra $B$, take $G_B=(u^*B,B,\operatorname{id})$ under [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison]. Its comma mapping formula is
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(H,G_B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,u^*B)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(A,u^*B)}\operatorname{Map}(F_A,B).$$
The first leg to the common base is the identity. Projection to the last factor is an equivalence: its homotopy fiber is the space of a point together with a path from it to a fixed point, which contracts to the constant path. Under this equivalence, Step 6's restriction map is exactly $h\mapsto u^*h\circ\eta_A$. Hence it is the desired equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(F_A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,u^*B)$. All maps used are restriction, composition and the natural comma comparison, so it is natural on the entire target algebra infinity category.

source.place: GH Remark A.4.2 and Propositions A.4.3--A.4.4; comma mapping formula

proof.text: Apply the dual coherent clause of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $T=u^*$. Steps 5--7 give a universal arrow $A\to u^*F_A$ for every $A$, with its mapping-space equivalence natural in the target algebra. The node assembles the universal arrows into a coherent functor $u_!$ and coherent unit, and gives the equivalence bifunctorially in $A,B$. The color values and identity-operation unit are the colimit comparisons in Step 5, and the operations are the substitutions in Step 4 as realized coherently by $H$.
